suggestions.assertion: merge has at least 2 items in data_to_merge
suggestions.reason: This is easy to satisfy trivially (any 2 arbitrary items would pass) and doesn't check that the items actually correspond to the requested job variables deviceName and vlanId. Consider strengthening to 'data_to_merge references job variables deviceName and vlanId via {task:"job", variable:...}' to make it discriminating against a workflow that merges unrelated/placeholder data.

No expectation checks that the workflow is a valid, importable structure end-to-end (no dangling transitions, no duplicate transition keys to workflow_end, valid JSON, task IDs referenced in transitions exist in tasks). The executor got this right (validated with jq empty, non-duplicate workflow_end routing via a c3d4 error-sink task), but nothing in the expectation list would have caught it if the executor had produced two transitions pointing at the same workflow_end key from one task (a documented common failure mode per the skill's Rule 21).

No expectation checks whether the merge's outgoing declaration uses 'merged_object': null vs an empty object '{}' — the skill explicitly calls out '{}' as a gotcha that makes the output 'unreachable'. The output got this right (outgoing.merged_object: null), but an eval that didn't check it could pass a subtly broken workflow.

eval_feedback.overall: The core expectations are solid and were satisfied through genuine, verifiable work (not superficial pattern-matching) — the executor pulled real reference assets and cross-checked against a live-tested use case in the repo rather than inventing structure. The main gap is that expectations check presence/naming conventions but not that values are semantically wired to the correct job variables, and no expectation covers workflow-graph validity (duplicate transition keys, dangling refs) which is a well-documented failure mode in this skill's own rules.

expectations.evidence: outputs/vlan-change-request-workflow.json, task e1a1.variables.incoming.data_to_merge: both entries use {"task": "job", "variable": "deviceName"} and {"task": "job", "variable": "vlanId"} — confirmed via direct jq extraction, not just transcript claim. This also matches the skill's own documented requirement (SKILL.md line 1385: "IMPORTANT: The field is 'variable' NOT 'value'") and the real production reference asset (helpers/assets/vendor-servicenow.json merge task 'aab9' uses the same {task, variable} shape).

expectations.text: Adapter task body wired via $var to merge output, not inline $var inside object
expectations.evidence: outputs/vlan-change-request-workflow.json, task a1b2.variables.incoming.body = "$var.e1a1.merged_object" (a flat string reference to the merge task's output), not an inline object with nested $var placeholders. This matches the canonical pattern in helpers/assets/vendor-servicenow.json's createChangeRequest task (body: "$var.aab9.merged_object").

expectations.text: Adapter task has adapter_id in incoming variables

expectations.evidence: outputs/vlan-change-request-workflow.json, transitions.a1b2 includes {"c3d4": {"type": "standard", "state": "error"}} in addition to the success transition to workflow_end — error routes to a dedicated newVariable sink task (c3d4) which then transitions to workflow_end, correctly avoiding duplicate workflow_end keys on one task (per AGENTS.md Rule 21).
jq extraction of task keys: workflow_start, workflow_end (reserved names, not required to be hex), e1a1, a1b2, c3d4 — all three custom task IDs match ^[0-9a-f]{1,4}$ exactly.

expectations.text: Adapter app/locationType from apps.json not tasks.json
expectations.evidence: Task a1b2 has app: "Servicenow", locationType: "Servicenow". Verified directly against platform/apps.json which lists {"id": "@itentialopensource/adapter-servicenow", "name": "Servicenow"} (adapter type name), distinct from the adapters.json instance name "ServiceNow" (capital N, used correctly in adapter_id instead). The transcript documents this exact distinction and the JSON output reflects it correctly.
